Hybrid debt instruments combine certain features of equity instruments and debt instruments. [sarb_circular_19_2004_capital_hybrid_instruments, p.1-2]

Banks issue these instruments with the objective of raising further qualifying capital for regulatory and supervisory purposes in a cost-effective manner. [sarb_circular_19_2004_capital_hybrid_instruments, p.1-2]

From a regulatory and supervisory perspective, banks wish to demonstrate that the instruments are deeply subordinated, noncumulative and perpetual, whereas from a tax perspective, banks wish to deduct the cost relating to the instruments from tax, resulting in interest, instead of dividends, being paid. The circular also discusses other capital instruments including preference shares, redeemable cumulative preference shares, and subordinated term debt. [sarb_circular_19_2004_capital_hybrid_instruments, p.13-15]

items.answer:
The 2014 Retail Distribution Review proposed an activity-based approach to categorizing intermediary services, distinguishing between advice (a service to the customer), intermediary services (services connecting product suppliers and customers), and other services provided by advisers and intermediaries (services to product suppliers). [fsca_rdr_2014, p.3-5]

The 2019 intermediary activity segmentation update built on this foundation by developing a more granular segmentation framework that demarcates between: Advice (a service to the customer); Other services to the customer; Services that truly "intermediate" between the customer and the insurer; Services to the insurer (split between binder services and other outsourced services); and Other services to the insurer not explicitly provided for in the current regulatory framework. [fsca_rdr_intermediary_segmentation_2019, p.2-3]

The 2019 update operationalized the RDR's structural interventions by implementing specific regulatory measures, including the capping of maximum binder fees that an insurer may pay to a non-mandated intermediary authorized to render advice at a maximum of 9% of applicable premiums if all binder functions are performed. [fsca_rdr_intermediary_segmentation_2019, p.2-3]

The 2019 update also introduced an insurer notification process to the FSCA in respect of arrangements where an insurer intends to pay remuneration to an independent intermediary or representative for functions other than services as intermediary or binder functions, including other outsourcing arrangements. [fsca_rdr_intermediary_segmentation_2019, p.2-3]
